moral.zh: 雨水和河流会从岩石中带走溶解的矿物离子，海底热液与火山活动也会带来或交换一些成分；水蒸发时盐大多留下，经过漫长岁月积累，并与海洋中的移除过程保持大致平衡。
moral.en: Rain and rivers carry dissolved mineral ions from rocks, while hydrothermal vents and volcanic activity also add or exchange some material. Most salts stay behind when water evaporates, accumulating over immense time while removal processes keep the ocean in a broad balance.

pages.en: A tiny drop of sea spray blew onto Xiaoshu's lips. He smacked them thoughtfully. “Oh, it’s salty! Where does all the saltiness in this enormous sea come from?”

pages.en: Xiaoshu spotted a small river flowing into the sea and thought of the fresh water in his cup. “Fresh water isn’t nearly this salty. Why is the ocean so salty when so many rivers flow into it?”

pages.zh: 爸爸从山上讲起：“雨落在岩石和土壤上，流水一点点冲刷、风化岩石，其中一些矿物成分会溶进水里，形成带电的微小粒子。科学家叫它们‘离子’。”
pages.en: Papa began in the mountains. “Rain falls on rocks and soil, and flowing water slowly weathers them. Some mineral components dissolve into the water as tiny charged particles called ions.”

pages.zh: “小溪汇成河流，河流每天都把很少量的离子送进海洋。河水里的离子很稀，所以不太咸；海洋却能在漫长岁月里把许多次微小的输入积累起来。”
pages.en: “Streams join into rivers, and every day rivers deliver tiny amounts of ions to the ocean. The ions are very dilute in river water, so it is not very salty. But the ocean can accumulate countless small deliveries over an immense span of time.”

pages.en: “Rivers are not the only source. At hydrothermal vents, seawater exchanges minerals with hot rock, and volcanic activity also supplies some material, adding to the ocean’s mix of ions.”

pages.en: “Sunlight turns some seawater into water vapor that returns to the air, but most dissolved salts do not evaporate with it. The water cycles again and again while most salts remain in the ocean.”

pages.en: After the tide went out, a tiny pool dried and left fine white crystals around the rock. Papa said, “Ocean life, sediments, and reactions with seafloor rock also remove some ions, so over long periods the amounts coming in and going out stay in a broad balance.”
